text.tspan: The browser will navigate away unless you stop it. Everything else hangs off that one decision.
invalid: no submit event fires at all
The browser shows its own bubble.
The browser serializes the form itself,
navigates to the action URL, and your
page is gone, taking any JavaScript
state with it. That is the default, and
it is the behavior to remember.
1. HTML attributes do most of it:
Only inputs with a name attribute are
included, and a disabled or unchecked
input is skipped. Turn it into a plain
pass it straight to fetch as the body.
Listen for submit on the FORM, never for click on the button: only submit
catches the Enter key. And client-side checks are for helpfulness, not safety:
anyone can bypass them, so the server must validate everything again.
